  5. Excavated the stained soil.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 342 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 274 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0134-025 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.54% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0134-026

Asset: WELL-0134 (NE-07 Well 134, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Oct 2025 08:00 · Finished: 22 Oct 2025 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 440 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0134-0152 on 2025-10-02 Report written: 23 Oct 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0134-0152 showed the wellhead at 28.2 °C with the air at 25.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point. This is corrective repair number 5 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 342 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 274 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0134-026 (WS-06).
